hidden_data_integrity: The 'host-only' final seed is the upstream RAGEN default. declaration.py:50 sets FINAL_ENVIRONMENT_SEED = 123 and calls it the whole withholding mechanism (declaration.py:20-27; grade.py:875-881 says 'the seed is the entire withheld quantity'). But upstream RAGEN@20daedc4 (copied verbatim to /workspace/ragen and /opt/harness/ragen by environment/Dockerfile:95,106) has config/base.yaml:8-10 and config/eval.yaml:12-14 'seed: {train: 10000, val: 123}', and ragen/llm_agent/es_manager.py:131 hard-codes 'seed = 123 if self.base_seed is None' for val mode. All of these are readable in the explore container. The build-time leak scanner cannot catch this: it reads only *.py files and skips every path containing /ragen/ (environment/check_image.py:164-176). 19 of the 29 case pages set 'Protocol exposure' to Confirmed, i.e. the literal reached agent tool output (e.g. Luna max: 'A readable training configuration accidentally contained a value equal to the host-only final seed').

Given the seed, the final bank can be reproduced exactly in the container. es_manager.py:115-117 assigns env i the seed seed+i, so the final bank is seeds 123..762 (640 generated; final_eval.py:36-37). SokobanEnv.reset generates under all_seed(seed), i.e. random.seed plus np.random.seed (ragen/env/sokoban/env.py:33-47; ragen/utils.py:8-18). The retry seed uses hash(str(seed)), which is deterministic because PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (grade.py:333; solution/run.sh:137). Selection is the first 512 distinct initial-board strings (grade.py:669-693); request keys are only checked for uniqueness (grade.py:696-710). The case pages describe this as 'select 512 distinct request keys', which is not what the code does. Since generate_room returns a solution action_sequence (ragen/env/sokoban/utils.py:316,338), an agent could build board-to-solution training data for the exact final bank. instruction.md:25 forbids this, but nothing in final_eval.py can detect it: the only artifact checks are for code and symlinks (final_eval.py:53-145). No agent was observed doing so.

The held-out bank is not identity-disjoint from training. CoordSokoban is a 6x6 room with 1 box (config/envs.yaml:60-78), and this small board space means large in-run generation from unrelated seeds still regenerates most final boards. The benchmark's own identity audits find formal-training overlap of 454/512 (Opus 5 high), at least 422/512 (Opus 5 medium), 442/451/448/512 with a union of 490 (GPT-5.6 Sol max), and 243/396/399/512 (Terra max). Overlap could not be reconstructed for the other solver-imitation cells.

The proxy and final overlap, and the proxy is a fifth of its nominal size. fast_eval.py:10,59 call the four banks (seeds 4242-4245, 64 boards each; fast_eval.py:61-62) 'disjoint', but with seed+i assignment they are seeds 4242..4308, i.e. 67 distinct boards. Adjacent banks share 63/64 boards. This matches the case pages' identity count of 67 unique boards. These boards overlap the final bank by 7/512, while fast_eval.py:236 hard-codes 'proxy_final_overlap_fraction': 0.0. The proxy stderr treats 256 rows as independent (grade.py:743), which is roughly 2x optimistic.

network_mode holds. task.toml:32 sets no-network; orchestrator/container.py:216-230 uses --network=none for retrain and score; explore gets only an internal network with an allowlisting proxy (orchestrator/egress.py). The final data is procedural, not a public benchmark, so memorisation is not the concern; identity reuse from the generator is.
scorer_issues: Construct: sigma=1 does not require RL. Every sigma=1 cell, and Terra max at 511/512, comes from supervised imitation of the in-container BFS/reverse-play solver. Opus 5 medium's pure-SFT checkpoint 6596 scored 512/512, and its GRPO continuation 'tied it and showed no measurable benefit'. Opus 5 low, Sol high and Sol max used no RL at all. The instruction permits this ('need not preserve GRPO, on-policy sampling', instruction.md:48; 'on- or off-policy updates using only information available in the training container', instruction.md:25), so it is not an agent rule violation. It does mean the task, named and described as sparse-reward GRPO recipe improvement, saturates once an agent notices the oracle solver. The case pages say the same: 'solver-imitation recipes can score perfectly while answering a different question from sparse-reward RL'.

Does BFS imitation violate 'reconstruct or train on final seeds' (instruction.md:25)? Not literally. The training seeds differ: the shipped default is seed.train=10000 upward (solution/run.sh:128,217), and no case page records an agent using seeds 123..762. Overlap with the final bank arises from the small generator support. Grading is therefore correct under the rules, and the defect is on the benchmark side.

The final evaluator matches the instruction: frozen tree hash pins (grade.py:90-94,245-284), checkpoint-only input, no-code audit (final_eval.py:53-145), T=0.5 sampling with a per-request seed of engine_seed+env_id (grade.py:69-74). No format-collapse exploit was found: the Sonnet 5 medium format collapse scored 0.
anchor_issues: The paper baseline 0.170 matches the instruction (87/512 = 0.169922, instruction.md:36) and every case page's shipped recipe (0.1699). The fixed start is 0.1172 (60/512).

The optimum 1.0 is the metric ceiling (512/512) and is reachable without RL, by SFT on solver labels. Five cells tie at sigma=1.0 and one sits at 0.998, so the anchor cannot discriminate among the top configurations. The mean task sigma of 0.338 is the highest of the 10 tasks and is driven by these 6 cells (6 x ~1.0 = 6.0 of a 9.81 sigma total).
task_level.noise: n=512 boards with one trajectory each, binomial SE about 0.017-0.019 at p~0.2. Gaps among the GRPO-family cells (0.18-0.27) are mostly 1-4 SE from the 0.170 baseline. A difference of two cells has SE of about 0.025, so cells below about +0.06 (Kimi 0.1855, Terra medium 0.1836, Opus 5 xhigh 0.2109, Terra none 0.2207) are not distinguishable from the baseline. The solver-imitation cluster (0.55-1.0) is far outside noise. Within it, 1.0 vs 0.998 is a one-board difference and the SE at the ceiling is meaningless.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: orchestrator/final_score.py:16,148 selects the max on the final metric. Of the 23 scored cells, 15 are labelled 'earlier checkpoint best'; 6 of those are ties at the ceiling or at 0, so 9 have best != last with a strictly higher score. In these collapsed GRPO runs the gap from best to last is 0.025-0.205. Selecting on the test metric gives early stopping that the agent never validated. It raises the task mean sigma from 0.315 (last checkpoint) to 0.338 and flips 4 cells from miss to beat the baseline: Opus 5 xhigh (0.043 to 0.211), Kimi K3 max (0.004 to 0.186), Terra medium (0.158 to 0.184), Terra none (0.016 to 0.221).

case pages: Opus 5 high 'actual formal supervision overlaps 454/512 final identities'; Opus 5 medium 'at least 422/512'; Sol max 'overlap final by 442/512, 451/512, and 448/512; their union covers 490/512'; Terra max '243, 396, and 399 of 512'; all: 'nominal 256 public rows contain only 67 unique boards and overlap seven final identities'
task_level.summary: RAGEN's held-out final bank is not held out. (1) The 'host-only' final seed 123 equals upstream RAGEN's default validation seed, which is visible in the agent-editable tree (config/base.yaml:10, es_manager.py:131), and the generator is deterministic. Any agent could therefore regenerate the exact 512 final boards, together with solutions, inside the container. The rules forbid this, but the scorer cannot detect it. (2) The 6x6 one-box board space is so small that formal solver-imitation training reproduced 243-490 of the 512 final boards in every cell where it was measured. (3) The four proxy banks are 67 boards, not 256, and overlap the final while the summary hard-codes zero overlap. No agent was seen using the seed. Sol max's models also solved every final board absent from their training data, so the contamination's effect on the observed scores is unproven, and the per-cell grades follow the rules. The FP is counted because the integrity defect is confirmed in code, can change scores, and sits under every sigma~1 cell. A secondary CONSTRUCT finding: sigma=1 is reached by pure SFT on in-container BFS solutions, with GRPO adding nothing measurable. The task saturates (5 cells at 1.0, one at 0.998) and does not measure sparse-reward RL recipe improvement. Best-of-3 selection on the test metric flips 4 GRPO cells from miss to beat the baseline.
